PIT.head: Advantage, the Penguins
PIT.body: Pittsburgh has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

CGY.head: The Flames face a real test

story.head: The Penguins are searching for answers
paras: The Penguins are on a four-game losing streak, and the Flames are winless in three (0-2-1). Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (24th in the NHL) and the Pens last in the Metropolitan (31st).

The Flames’ record (.440) is about what their chances are worth. The Penguins have played better than their record (.348) says: their chances are worth about .534, and their finishing has held them back.

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and take more penalties than they draw (29th). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so the Penguins wait for good looks, but they settle for hopeful ones. Calgary has scored 2.44 goals a game, the fewest in the league. As for the Penguins, they sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Penguins are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 12 A / 19 P in 25 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (6 G / 11 A / 17 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Tommy Novak (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 23 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Dustin Wolf (5-6-2 / .877 SV% in 13 GS) is expected to start for Calgary, and Artūrs Šilovs (5-8-1 / .878 SV% in 14 GS) for Pittsburgh.

At home, Dan Muse likes to send McGroarty, Lapierre and Koivunen out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Suniev, Castagna and Tsyplakov. One more thing: the Penguins usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.
